release.summary: Crest 0.7 brings Chromium and WebKit together in one Mac app, with Chromium as the default and a shared browser core across Mac, iPhone, and iPad.
added: Run Chrome Web Store extensions in each Mac Space, including popups, side panels, shortcuts, and supported native companion apps.

added.text: Choose Chromium or WebKit for new pages, one page, or a website. Use WebKit for Reader, whole-page translation, built-in blocking, and supported FairPlay video.
Pause and resume Chromium downloads, including interrupted transfers when the server supports recovery.

added: Receive local service-worker and extension notifications while Crest runs, with Space access and notification permissions respected.
changed: Use one browser core for Space isolation, navigation, persistence, permissions, and synchronization across the Apple apps.

changed.text: Inspect Chromium pages with DevTools and save them as MHTML archives; WebKit keeps Web Inspector and web archives.

changed: Check the exact release source and both platform builds before signing and publication.

fixed.text: Resume interrupted Chromium profile upgrades without losing track of existing profiles.

fixed: Honor unsaved-changes prompts before switching engines or restarting for an update.
Refuse unavailable page actions during engine startup instead of running them later unexpectedly.

fixed.text: Advertise the macOS version required by the whole app when offering updates.

upgrading: Mac requires Apple silicon and macOS 26.1 or later. iPhone and iPad continue to use WebKit on iOS and iPadOS 26.1 or later.

upgrading.text: Spaces, tabs, history, and Crest Passwords carry over from the previous stable release. Chromium and WebKit keep separate website data, so switching engines can require signing in again.

upgrading: Reinstall older WebKit extensions from the Chrome Web Store in the Spaces where you want them.
See the [engine guide](https://crestbrowser.com/guides/engines/) for feature differences, screen-sharing limits, and notification support.

entries.message: Protected-video pages still switch to WebKit automatically. Engine switches respect unsaved-changes prompts and remember the website only after the move is allowed.
Interrupted Chromium profile upgrades resume safely without losing track of your existing browsing profiles.
Pause and resume Chromium downloads, and recover interrupted transfers when the server supports it.
Chromium can show local service-worker and extension notifications while Crest runs, with Space access and notification permissions respected.
Validate the exact source before release, build the current native core with the Chromium host, and make startup cancellation and deferred requests explicit.
Crest updates advertise the macOS version the whole app requires, so older Macs are not offered an incompatible update.
Crest 0.7 brings Chromium and WebKit together on Mac, with Chrome Web Store extensions and engine choices for each website. iPhone and iPad continue to use WebKit.
